# Cases from jq's test suites that jqgo deliberately does not follow.
# Each "## " line gives the reason for the programs listed under it.

## modules (import/include/modulemeta) are not supported
import "a" as foo; import "b" as bar; def fooa: foo::a; [fooa, bar::a, bar::b, foo::a]
import "c" as foo; [foo::a, foo::c]
include "c"; [a, c]
import "data" as $e; import "data" as $d; [$d[].this,$e[].that,$d::d[].this,$e::e[].that]|join(";")
import "data" as $a; import "data" as $b; def f: {$a, $b}; f
include "shadow1"; e
include "shadow1"; include "shadow2"; e
import "shadow1" as f; import "shadow2" as f; import "shadow1" as e; [e::e, f::e]
modulemeta
modulemeta | .deps | length
modulemeta | .defs | length
import "test_bind_order" as check; check::check

## jqgo keeps integers exact in 64 bits; jq rounds them to doubles
. - 10
.[0] - 10
.x - 10
.[] as $n | $n+0 | [., tostring, . == $n]

## jq 1.7 preserves number literals (1.000, big integers); jqgo normalizes numbers
[., tojson]
map([., . == 1]) | tojson
. as $big | [$big, $big + 1] | map(. > 10000000000000000000000000000000)

## Go's RE2 differs from Oniguruma: no lookaround, ASCII-only \b, unmatched
## empty groups, and empty matches right after a previous match
[match("( )*"; "g")]
[match(".+?\\b")]
gsub("(?=u)"; "u")
gsub("[^a-z]*(?<x>[a-z]*)"; "Z\(.x)")

## jq quirks: fromjson accepting "nan1234", input's error text in jq's test harness
fromjson | isnan
try input catch .
